Series::LinearAlgAccessor::cholesky_inverse¶

Back to Series::LinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::LinearAlgAccessor::cholesky_inverse(bool upper = false) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::cholesky_inverse(bool upper = false) const

What It Does¶

Builds A^-1 from the owning Cholesky factor. Lower mode interprets the owner as L in A=L L^T; upper mode interprets it as U in A=U^T U.

Inverting The Represented SPD Matrix¶

The method solves against every column of the identity, sharing one triangular factor across all columns. The result is symmetric. Use it when the inverse is itself required; for A X=B, cholesky_solve() avoids materializing a dense inverse and is usually the stronger numerical choice.

Parameter And Shape¶

upper selects the factor orientation and must match the original Cholesky call. Input [...,n,n] produces [...,n,n], preserving batch dimensions.

Gradient¶

Reverse mode applies the inverse rule through L L^T or U^T U and returns a sensitivity only in the factor’s active triangle.

Example¶

auto a = pluss::make_series({{4.0, 2.0}, {2.0, 3.0}});
auto l = a.linearalg.cholesky();
auto inverse = l.linearalg.cholesky_inverse();
std::cout << inverse << "\n";
std::cout << a.linearalg.mm(inverse) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.375, -0.25],
  [-0.25, 0.5]]
pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0],
  [1.6653345e-16, 1]]

The tiny off-diagonal residual is floating-point roundoff, not a failure of the inverse identity.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Pass the factor, not the original SPD matrix.

  • upper changes the represented product; it is not merely an output-format toggle.

  • An inverse is more expensive and often less stable than solving directly.

See Also¶

  • cholesky: compute the factor.

  • cholesky_solve: solve without forming an inverse.
